ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, what is the sum of $\angle A+\angle B+\angle C+\angle D$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Draw lines AD and BC.\\
In quadrilateral ABCD, we have $\angle DAE + \angle EAB + \angle ABF + \angle FBC + \angle DCF + \angle BCF + \angle CDE + \angle ADE = 360^\circ$,\\
Since $\angle DEA = 105^\circ$ and $\angle BFC = 120^\circ$,\\
It follows that $\angle DAE + \angle ADE = 180^\circ - 105^\circ = 75^\circ$ and $\angle FBC + \angle BCF = 180^\circ - 120^\circ = 60^\circ$,\\
Therefore, $\angle EAB + \angle ABF + \angle DCF + \angle CDE = 360^\circ - 75^\circ - 60^\circ = 225^\circ$.\\
Hence, $\angle A + \angle B + \angle C + \angle D = \boxed{225^\circ}$.

Read from the question that the required quantity is the sum of the four labeled corner angles at A, B, C, D, namely ∠EAB + ∠ABF + ∠DCF + ∠CDE. Draw auxiliary segments AD and BC to form quadrilateral ABCD. The angle sum of quadrilateral ABCD is 360°. Its four angles split into the desired four angles plus two extra pairs: at A and D the pair ∠DAE + ∠ADE, and at B and C the pair ∠FBC + ∠BCF.
